findings.body: Legacy independently applies the update to its own old state instead of receiving the object successfully written to storage, so the two stores can diverge or legacy can reject an update that storage accepted.
findings.evidence: _, _, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, createValidation, updateValidation, forceAllowCreate, options)
findings.failure_mode: The asynchronous secondary write can produce a different object or error despite a successful primary write.
findings.impact: Legacy independently applies the update to its own old state instead of receiving the object successfully written to storage, so the two stores can diverge or legacy can reject an update that storage accepted.
findings.root_cause: The patch reuses the original UpdatedObjectInfo for the second write rather than forwarding the authoritative storage result.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the successful storage result in updateWrapper and pass that wrapper to Legacy.Update, preserving the upstream preconditions while making the updated object deterministic.
findings.title: Preserve the storage result when asynchronously updating legacy storage
findings.trigger: A mode 3 update uses an UpdatedObjectInfo that computes a patch or replacement from the old object, while the legacy store is behind or differs from storage.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 139 shows d.Legacy.Update passes objInfo directly instead of wrapping the storage result. The old code (L101-104) used updateWrapper with the updated object. The patch removes this wrapper, so legacy computes its own update from its old state rather than receiving the authoritative storage result, causing potential divergence.

findings.body: The failure is recorded in the legacy-duration histogram using a storage start time, while the storage-duration histogram has no error observation; storage failure dashboards and latency data are incorrect.
findings.failure_mode: Monitoring attributes primary storage failures to the wrong backend and omits them from the correct metric.
findings.impact: The failure is recorded in the legacy-duration histogram using a storage start time, while the storage-duration histogram has no error observation; storage failure dashboards and latency data are incorrect.
findings.root_cause: The storage-create error branch invokes the legacy metric recorder instead of the storage metric recorder.
findings.suggested_fix: Call recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) on this error path.
findings.title: Record storage-create failures in the storage metric
findings.trigger: Storage.Create returns an error in mode 3.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 45 shows d.recordLegacyDuration called when Storage.Create fails. The function name and metrics.go:54-56 confirm this records to the legacy histogram, but the error is from storage. Should be recordStorageDuration.

findings.body: The metric's `kind` label contains the object name, causing high-cardinality series and making delete duration metrics inconsistent with all other operations.
findings.failure_mode: Metrics aggregation and dashboards by resource kind produce incorrect or unbounded results.
findings.impact: The metric's `kind` label contains the object name, causing high-cardinality series and making delete duration metrics inconsistent with all other operations.
findings.root_cause: The delete success path supplies the request name to the metric parameter defined as `kind`.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass options.Kind as the label value instead of name.
findings.title: Use the resource kind rather than the object name for delete metrics
findings.trigger: A successful mode 3 delete is performed for any object name.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 106 shows d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) where 'name' is the object name passed as the 'kind' parameter. Comparing to line 103 which correctly uses options.Kind, this creates high-cardinality metrics with object names as labels.

findings.body: The legacy collection-delete duration is recorded as storage duration, while the legacy histogram misses the operation and storage metrics contain false observations.
findings.evidence: d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)
findings.failure_mode: Backend-specific collection-delete monitoring reports the operation under the wrong backend.
findings.impact: The legacy collection-delete duration is recorded as storage duration, while the legacy histogram misses the operation and storage metrics contain false observations.
findings.root_cause: The legacy delete-collection goroutine invokes the storage metric recorder.
findings.suggested_fix: Call recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy).
findings.title: Record asynchronous collection deletes in the legacy metric
findings.trigger: The asynchronous Legacy.DeleteCollection call completes, either successfully or with an error.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 166 shows d.recordStorageDuration called inside the legacy DeleteCollection goroutine with startLegacy timer. This records a legacy operation to the storage histogram. Should be recordLegacyDuration.

findings.body: Those downstream logs lose the `name`, `kind`, and `method` fields assembled in `log`, making delete failures harder to correlate and diagnose.

pr.body:
**What is this feature?**

Mode 3 will work the following way:

reads (get, list) : only use unified storage
writes (create, update, delete, delete-collection) : write to unified storage and then asynchronously, write to legacy, just as a safe measure.

**Why do we need this feature?**

[Add a description of the problem the feature is trying to solve.]

**Who is this feature for?**

[Add information on what kind of user the feature is for.]

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

Fixes https://github.com/grafana/search-and-storage-team/issues/53

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

Please check that:
- [ ] It works as expected from a user's perspective.

The context receives the un-enriched d.Log instead of the enriched 'log', losing operation identifiers in downstream context-aware logging.

validated_findings.body: The test can pass without verifying that the legacy write occurred, so regressions in the core dual-write behavior remain undetected; the same gap exists for the added update, delete, and delete-collection tests.
validated_findings.evidence: obj, err := dw.Create(context.Background(), tt.input, func(context.Context, runtime.Object) error { return nil }, &metav1.CreateOptions{})
validated_findings.failure_mode: The test suite provides false confidence about mode 3's secondary writes and can finish before those writes execute.
validated_findings.impact: The test can pass without verifying that the legacy write occurred, so regressions in the core dual-write behavior remain undetected; the same gap exists for the added update, delete, and delete-collection tests.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new tests assert only the synchronous storage result and never synchronize with or verify the asynchronous legacy goroutines.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use a channel or mock callback to wait for the asynchronous legacy operation, then assert its invocation, arguments, and error handling for each mode 3 write method.
validated_findings.title: Synchronize and assert asynchronous legacy writes in mode 3 tests
validated_findings.trigger: The mode 3 implementation fails to invoke, cancels, misorders, or passes incorrect data to the asynchronous legacy create; the test returns immediately after the synchronous call.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage gap observation rather than a bug in the production code. The tests verify synchronous behavior correctly. While better async verification would improve test quality, the absence of such verification is a test improvement suggestion, not a defect introduced by the patch.
